title: F · Smart money inside Polymarket
decision: Pivot: fair-value / mispricing helper; refine the topic.

experiments.title: Dataset overview
experiments.question: What does the data cover, and do enough wallets trade many markets to measure skill?
experiments.headline: 300 markets in 294 events, 489,682 trades by 56,852 wallets; 1,877 wallets traded 5+ markets and the top 1% of wallets did 61% of the volume.
notes: Trade rows are participant records: each fill appears once for every wallet in it.

experiments.title: Calibration and fair value (H0)
experiments.question: Do YES prices match how often YES happens, and can a simple recalibration improve them?
experiments.headline: Prices are off by 6.6% on average across buckets; the fair-value map (b = 0.89) does not improve period-B log loss (0.5040 → 0.5102).
notes: Fair value is fitted on period A only and used for every edge measure in E2–E4.
Points from different horizons of the same market are not independent.

experiments.title: Skill persistence (H1)
experiments.question: Do wallets with high edge in earlier markets also have high edge in later markets?
experiments.headline: Spearman ρ between period-A and period-B edge = 0.086 (95% CI -0.106 to 0.267, permutation p = 0.1588, 129 wallets with ≥ 5 markets in each period). Holding long-shot style fixed: ρ = 0.085.
notes: Pass rule (pre-registered): ρ > 0 with permutation p < 0.05; fewer than 30 wallets = inconclusive.
Edge is measured against fair value from E1; the raw-price version is reported for comparison.

experiments.title: Information in skilled wallets' trades (H2)
experiments.question: Is the price more likely to move in a trade's direction when the trader has proven skill?
experiments.headline: Top-tier trades beat other trades by +0.39 points to resolution (95% CI -3.97 to +4.87; 128 markets, 125 events).
notes: Skill tier is decided with markets closed before each trade (walk-forward).
Main test (pre-registered): trades with YES price in the band, equal weight, to resolution; per-market differences, bootstrap over events. Fewer than 5 events or 10 markets = inconclusive.

experiments.title: Copy-trading backtest (H3)
experiments.question: After realistic delay and costs, does following skilled wallets make money?
experiments.headline: Copying top-tier wallets 60 min later with a 1¢ cost returns -3.8% per $1 (95% CI -16.2% to +8.1%; 1678 copies in 124 markets) vs -2.7% for other ranked wallets.
notes: Signals: top-tier trades of at least $100 with YES price in (0.05, 0.95), one per wallet/market/hour; entry at the last price after the delay plus the cost; held to resolution.
Pass rule (pre-registered): 60-minute delay, 1¢ cost, mean > 0 with CI above 0.
